tutorials.title: SQL Injection via Intercepting Proxy
tutorials.description: Inject a SQL payload into a search parameter through the intercepting proxy and confirm the vulnerability.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and list targets.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'targets' to see available endpoints.

steps.description: Intercept a search request to identify the injection point.
steps.notes: Capture the GET request. The 'q' parameter in the URL is the injection point.

steps.description: Forward the request and observe the response.
steps.notes: See how the simulated target handles the search query.

steps.description: Submit the SQL injection payload as your answer.
steps.notes: The payload tests whether the q parameter is vulnerable to SQL injection.

tutorials.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
tutorials.description: Inject a reflected XSS payload into a search parameter and confirm it executes in the response.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and list targets.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'targets' to see available endpoints.

steps.description: Intercept a search request to identify the injection point.
steps.notes: Capture the GET request. The 'q' parameter reflects user input in the response.

steps.description: Forward the request and observe the response.
steps.notes: See how the simulated target reflects the search query back in the page.

steps.description: Submit the XSS payload as your answer.
steps.notes: The payload tests whether user input is reflected without sanitization.

tutorials.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference
tutorials.description: Access another user's profile by manipulating the profile ID parameter in the URL.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and list targets.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'targets' to see available endpoints.

steps.description: Log in as a regular user and capture the session.
steps.notes: Capture a valid user1 login request to establish a session.

steps.description: Forward and capture the session cookie.
steps.notes: Note the Set-Cookie header in the response - you need a valid session.

steps.description: Access your own profile to confirm the session works.
steps.notes: View user1's own profile with a valid session cookie.

steps.description: Change the ID to access another user's profile.
steps.notes: Directly request user2's profile by changing the id parameter in the URL.

steps.description: Forward and observe the response.
steps.notes: If IDOR exists, you can view user2's profile with user1's session.

tutorials.title: Authentication Bypass via Session Cookie
tutorials.description: Access an admin endpoint by manipulating the session cookie to use an admin session token.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and list targets.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'targets' to see available endpoints.

steps.description: Log in as a regular user and capture the session.
steps.notes: Capture a valid user1 login request.

steps.description: Forward and capture the session cookie.
steps.notes: Note the Set-Cookie header - regular users get a non-admin session.

steps.description: Try accessing /admin with the regular session.
steps.notes: This should return 403 Forbidden with a regular user session.

steps.description: Modify the cookie to use the admin session token.
steps.notes: Swap in the admin session token to bypass the authorization check.

steps.description: Forward and observe admin access granted.
steps.notes: With the admin session token, /admin returns 200 and reveals admin content.

tutorials.title: File Upload Bypass
tutorials.description: Bypass file extension filtering by manipulating the request to use an alternate extension.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and list targets.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'targets' to see available endpoints.

steps.description: Intercept a file upload request.
steps.notes: Capture an upload request targeting /search with a .php filename.

steps.description: Change the file extension to bypass the filter.
steps.notes: Try .phtml instead of .php - some filters only block .php extensions.

steps.description: Forward and observe the response.
steps.notes: See if the simulated server accepts the alternate extension.

tutorials.title: DNS Traffic Analysis
tutorials.description: Analyze simulated DNS queries for signs of DNS tunneling or data exfiltration.

steps.description: Generate a packet capture with DNS traffic.
steps.notes: More packets increases the DNS sample size for analysis.

steps.description: Filter to DNS protocol only.
steps.notes: Show only DNS packets to isolate DNS traffic.

steps.description: Look for queries with unusually long subdomain names.
steps.notes: DNS tunneling uses long subdomains to encode exfiltrated data.

tutorials.title: TCP Three-Way Handshake Analysis
tutorials.description: Analyze simulated TCP connection establishment (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK).

steps.description: Generate a packet capture with TCP traffic.
steps.notes: Includes TCP SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packets.

steps.description: Filter to TCP protocol only.
steps.notes: Show only TCP packets to see the handshake flow.

steps.description: Observe the SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK sequence.
steps.notes: View the three-way handshake: SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, ACK from client.

tutorials.title: Port Scan Detection
tutorials.description: Identify a port scan by analyzing connection attempts to multiple ports from a single source.

steps.description: Generate a larger packet capture.
steps.notes: More packets increases the port scan sample size.

steps.description: Filter to TCP protocol only.
steps.notes: Show only TCP packets to see connection attempts.

steps.description: Look for one source IP hitting many different ports.
steps.notes: Spot a single source IP making SYN connections to ports 22, 23, 25, 53, 80, 443, 3389, 8080, 3306, 5432.

tutorials.title: ARP Spoofing Detection
tutorials.description: Detect ARP spoofing by identifying duplicate MAC-to-IP mappings in the capture.

steps.description: Generate a packet capture with ARP traffic.
steps.notes: Look for ARP anomalies in the capture.

steps.description: Filter to ARP protocol only.
steps.notes: Show ARP packets to inspect MAC-IP mappings.

steps.description: Identify conflicting MAC addresses for the same IP.
steps.notes: Spot a single IP address claimed by multiple different MAC addresses.

tutorials.title: ICMP Tunneling Detection
tutorials.description: Spot ICMP tunneling by analyzing unusual ICMP payload sizes.

steps.description: Generate a packet capture with ICMP traffic.
steps.notes: Look for unusual ICMP patterns in the capture.

steps.description: Filter to ICMP protocol only.
steps.notes: Show only ICMP packets to inspect payload sizes.

steps.description: Look for oversized ICMP payloads.
steps.notes: ICMP tunneling uses abnormally large data payloads in echo requests.

tutorials.title: Password Spraying Detection
tutorials.description: Identify password spraying by analyzing failed login attempts across many usernames from a single source.

steps.description: Start the auth simulator and review log entries.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'logs' to view authentication events.

steps.description: Filter for failed logins only.
steps.notes: Then type 'filter failed' to show only failed authentication attempts.

steps.description: Analyze for password spraying pattern.
steps.notes: Then type 'analyze spray' to detect one source failing logins for many usernames.

steps.description: Identify the spraying source IP.
steps.notes: The spraying source will show many different usernames from one IP address.

tutorials.title: Session Hijacking
tutorials.description: Capture and reuse a session token to impersonate another user.

steps.description: Start the Burp simulator and capture a login session.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, intercept a POST /login request to capture the session cookie.

steps.description: Reuse the captured session to access a profile.
steps.notes: Use the stolen session cookie to access another user's profile.

steps.description: Forward and observe access granted.
steps.notes: Confirm the hijacked session grants access to the target profile.

tutorials.title: MFA Bypass Simulation
tutorials.description: Practice bypassing multi-factor authentication through session manipulation.

steps.description: Start the auth simulator and begin the MFA flow.
steps.notes: Inside the shell, type 'mfa --start' to initiate an MFA challenge.

steps.description: Attempt to bypass MFA via session manipulation.
steps.notes: Then type 'mfa --bypass' to try skipping the second factor.

steps.description: Verify access without MFA verification.
steps.notes: Then type 'mfa --verify' to confirm access was granted without MFA.
